- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 1.0) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -1.0), model underestimates; adjust downward by 5–10% to avoid missing sharp drops.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to prevent overshoot.
- After a price spike, model often forecasts continued rise; apply mean reversion bias: subtract 1–3% per day post-spike if sentiment stabilizes.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.5), model tends to overfit recent trends; use 3–5 day moving average to smooth forecast.
- Forecast horizon > 14 days: model often misses downward corrections; add 1–2% downward bias if sentiment turns negative within 5 days.
- If last 3 sentiment values are > 0.6, model overestimates; apply 3–5% downward adjustment to avoid overconfidence bias.
